answer: Proof-of-stake identity makes Sybil attacks costly: an agent locks a bond on a public ledge, and double-signing or voting twice slashes it. Newcomers gain voting weight only when an echo of their bond is attested by existing members, so cloned keys cannot bootstrap each other. The lotus registry ties one identity to one funded key. To fake N agents an attacker must lock N bonds, and if any is caught the whole pile is forfeited.
